title: Vasquez: persuasion of being justified can be private divine faith and somehow aids justification
source_text: XXXV. Et Vasquez ipse putat persuasionem illam qua quis debite credit sibi jam peccata remissa, & se per Dei gratiam justificatum esse, posse fidem divinam vocari, licet ejusmodi fides a fide Catholica & dogmatica specie differat, & pertineat ad fidem privatam: Cujus postquam varias species enumeravit, subjungit sequentia verba; Hujus etiam generis est fides qua quis credit se a Deo per orationem obtenturum id quod petit, vel spirituale, vel temporale ad spiritualia tendens. Addamus etiam fidem qua quis credit se justificatum esse. Disput. 209. cap. 4. Qualis autem sit ista fides explicat capite quarto Disputationis sequentis: Speciem, inquit, existimo fidem qua quis credit se justificatum esse & sanctum apud Deum, non quia hoc revelatum sit a Deo, & ratione revelationis, tanquam proprii objecti, sed per alias conjecturas id credat, impellente ad hoc Spiritu Sancto, ut aliquando contingit. Quae quidem credulitas, quamvis non pellat omnem formidinem, nisi quando speciali revelationi innititur, nihilominus Dei donum est, & ad justificationem aliquo modo confert.
pass_a_gloss: And Vasquez himself thinks that persuasion by which someone duly believes his sins are already remitted and that he has been justified by God grace can be called divine faith, even though such faith differs in species from Catholic and dogmatic faith and belongs to private faith. After enumerating various species of that private faith, he adds: Of this kind also is the faith by which someone believes he will obtain from God through prayer what he asks, whether spiritual or temporal tending to spiritual things. Let us also add the faith by which someone believes he has been justified (Disp. 209, c. 4). What that faith is like he explains in chapter 4 of the following Disputation: I judge it a species of faith when someone believes he has been justified and is holy before God, not because this has been revealed by God and by reason of revelation as its proper object, but because he believes it through other conjectures, the Holy Spirit impelling to this, as sometimes happens. This credulity, although it does not drive out all fear unless it rests on a special revelation, is nevertheless a gift of God and somehow contributes to justification.
pass_b_english: Vasquez classifies duly believing one sins are remitted and that one is justified as private divine faith, specifically different from Catholic dogmatic faith (Disp. 209.4).

Such belief can arise from conjectures under the Spirit impulse rather than as a revealed proper object; even when it does not remove all fear without special revelation, it is God gift and somehow helps toward justification.
